info.encodingsQuestion: How do legacy encodings differ from standard Unicode?
info.legacyDescription: The stored data consists of ASCII characters. Without the corresponding font, the underlying characters are shown directly, so the matching legacy font is needed to display them as Sinhala glyphs.
info.fmFontsHint: SinhalaFonts.net has FM Abhaya, FM Malithi, FM Gemunu, FM Bindumathi, and other legacy FM fonts, with previews and downloads. Availability on a third-party site does not imply an open license; follow each font's own terms.
info.pitakaHint: Pitaka.lk provides Unicode versions that preserve traditional FM designs while supporting standard Sinhala text. Fonts are available for download and installation; commercial use still requires the appropriate permission.
info.unicodeDescription: Modern operating systems usually include Sinhala fonts. The text uses standard Unicode Sinhala characters with defined meaning.
info.systemFontsHint: Default fonts vary by operating system. Common choices are listed below.
info.windowsFonts: Nirmala UI is a sans-serif UI font for Windows 8 and later. Iskoola Pota has a more traditional text style and was the earlier Windows default for Sinhala. Since Windows 10, it is a supplemental Sinhala font, usually installed with language support.
info.appleFonts: Sinhala Sangam MN has a modern sans-serif / UI style, while Sinhala MN has a traditional text style. Apple supplies both but does not explicitly define them as a serif/sans-serif system fallback pair.
info.androidFonts: Noto Sans Sinhala is a sans-serif font, usually used as the main system fallback for Sinhala. Noto Serif Sinhala is a serif font and is explicitly configured as a serif fallback in AOSP. Android vendors may change the system font configuration, so the actual fonts can vary.
info.converterTitle: About the Sinhala font encoding converter
info.converterDescription: Unlike simple character replacement tools, this converter does more than substitute characters one by one using a mapping table. It recognizes how consonants, vowel signs, joiners, reduced consonant forms and conjunct glyphs combine, reorders the characters and reconstructs the corresponding structures. Reverse conversion regenerates glyph sequences according to the legacy font's encoding rules.
info.examplesHint: The examples below illustrate the main conversion rules supported by the converter, comparing FM Abhaya and Unicode encodings and glyphs. Click “Show underlying encoding” to see the actual character sequences behind the FM glyphs.
info.vowelsDescription: Converts pre-base, post-base and variant combinations of legacy vowel signs into Unicode logical character order.
info.conjunctsDescription: Supports traditional conjuncts still used in modern Sinhala, as well as complex conjuncts and touching forms found in Pali, classical texts and traditional typesetting.
info.paliVowelsDescription: For Pali written in Sinhala script, changes ඒ, ඕ and their vowel signs to the written forms එ, ඔ while retaining consonant viramas. Off by default; not suitable for ordinary Sinhala text.
info.conjunctAvailability: ඤ්‍ජ, ණ්‍ඩ, ම්‍බ and ඞ්ග share legacy codes with prenasalized consonants, so information about their original conjunct forms is lost when converting back to Unicode.
info.glyphsDescription: Prenasalized consonants use their dedicated codes; some combinations containing ද have optional compact glyphs.
info.reducedDescription: Controls යංශය (yansaya), රකාරාංශය (rakaaraansaya) and රේඵය (repaya) separately. Current reduced forms are preserved by default; with preservation off, each form can be uniformly applied or expanded.
info.mixedDescription: Only recognized Sinhala segments in mixed text are converted; English, numbers and text in other languages remain unchanged.
info.orderDescription: Different legacy input orders for the same glyph combination map to a single standard Unicode character sequence.
info.vowelOrder: Code order of Rakaaraansaya and vowel signs
info.longVowelOrder: Code order of Rakaaraansaya and the long-vowel sign
info.legacyScopeTitle: About the legacy font encoding referred to on this website
info.legacyScopeDescription: Legacy font encodings have no single standard, and character mappings may differ between fonts. Since the FM family, including FM Abhaya, FM Malithi and FM Gemunu, was widely used in the early digitization of Sinhala, “Sinhala legacy font encoding” on this website refers to the character mappings of FM fonts unless otherwise stated. Some sections refer specifically to the mapping rules of FM Abhaya.
info.fontsTitle: About the FM family fonts used on this website
info.fontsQuestion: Are these original fonts? Are there copyright or usage-rights risks?
info.fontsPrefix: Glyph previews in the legacy editor and encoding introduction use built-in legacy-compatible fonts based on Abhaya Libre and Gemunu Libre (see
info.fontsSuffix: ). They only simulate legacy font character mappings and are not the original FM Abhaya or Gemunu fonts.

info.optionsDescription: Common conjuncts, rare conjuncts and touching forms have separate controls. Current conjunct forms are preserved by default; with preservation off, conversion follows the selected options and prioritizes dedicated FM conjunct glyphs in legacy output.
info.conjunctComparisonNote: Expanded forms and their corresponding conjunct glyphs.
info.compactHint: Requires the corresponding option; off by default
info.touchingDescription: Touching forms use consonant + ZWJ + virama + consonant; ligated conjuncts use consonant + virama + ZWJ + consonant.

notes.title: Notes
notes.quotes: Legacy fonts usually do not support straight quotes; conversion automatically replaces them with curly quotes.
notes.vowelCodes: Legacy encoding cannot distinguish “්‍රු / ◌්‍රූ” from “්‍රැ / ◌්‍රෑ”; both are displayed as “්‍රැ / ◌්‍රෑ”.
notes.missingGlyphs: Legacy encoding lacks dedicated glyphs for “ඞ”, “ඞි” and “ඞී”, so they cannot be converted.
notes.partialSupport: Only some fonts support the legacy code for “ඣ්”; others may display it incorrectly.
notes.touchingLetters: Unicode supports generating touching forms, but legacy encoding has no corresponding slots and displays the letters separately. Original touching layout cannot be preserved and must be regenerated according to the settings.
notes.exportFonts: Exported Unicode Sinhala text uses system fonts, with Iskoola Pota as the fallback.
notes.documentLayout: DOCX keeps editable paragraphs and images. PDF body text reflows as paragraphs, retaining font sizes, indents, alignment and page breaks where possible. Slide PDFs can be exported as PPTX with editable text boxes in their page positions. Target fonts may change wrapping and pagination.
